sec.p: About the ORKG The OPEN RESERARCH KNOWLEDGE GRAPH (ORKG)- is a Knowledge Graph that will lunch the classical scientific publication exposure into a bidirectional user-knowledge relation, that is also machine actionable. This more dynamic relation is empowered through structured knowledge capsules called COMPARISONS, provided by users. The users can predigest additional information into existing comparisons and exploit the available possibilities provided by the ORKG platform. About Smart review (SR) Smart Reviews (SM) is a document that contains a set of published comparisons in the ORKG. This format allows to integrate, explain and interlink information from the comparisons. It also gives the opportunity to discuss visualizations. About comparisons All comparisons have a dark grey column on the left; this column is dedicated to the properties whose object is reported in every CONTRIBUTION -vertical columns-. In the comparisons presented here the structure underlying every contribution (one publication can have more than one contribution) is separated under two major sets of properties: Has system qualities and Has system measurements; -please check on the "graph view" of any contribution-. Under Has system qualities there is a glossary of qualities :Atomic, Plasma and Spectroscopy characteristics, and quality types. Under Has system measurements there are listed all the measurable quality types appending the word "measurement" .

sec.title: About this Smart Review (SR) : The spectrum originated from highly charged ions (HCI) produced in laboratory experiments, and space observation

p.p:
The broader line of research of this SR is
X-ray radiation originated from Highly Charged Ions(HCI)
. HCIs can be produced in the laboratory as well as observed in the cosmos. The information presented in the SR showcases: observational, experimental, modeling and theoretical, as well as some outlook and review publications. All the publications can fit well within the new field of X-ray Astronomy and the general field of Plasma Spectroscopy. This SR is part of a series of three, listed in the table below. TABLE 1

p.p:
The spectrum originated from highly charged ions (HCI) produced in laboratory experiments, and space observations
Transition energies of highly charged ions is a topic of much interest in atomic physics. In the laboratory, the production of HCIs requires high technology plasma sources and precision measurements from dedicated spectrometers. The emission is also of utmost interest for the interpretation of the spectrum from astrophysical sources; hence fundamental for the designing of tasks of recent and future space observatories. Here is the list of four comparisons that present the richness of the HCIs spectrum and highlights the collaboration between laboratory measurements and space observations of cosmic sources. TABLE 2

sec.title: Transition energies of highly charged ions (HCI) produced in an electron beam ion trap (EBIT), for the purpose of Quantum Electrodynamic (QED) studies.

p.p: The precision measurement of wavelengths in hydrogen-like HCIs is complementary to wavelength measurements using neutral hydrogen Phys. Rev. Lett. 92, 230802 – 2004 [@10.1103/PhysRevLett.92.230802]. However, with enough spectral resolution the Lamb shift is measurable in Hy- like and He-like where the S states have a dominant presence, hence can probe the finite size of the nucleus. In a quote by [@10.1088/0953-4075/43/7/074021] "….a much lower resolution is required to probe the same physics (or to go beyond it) when working with highly charged ions …. “

The comparisons in this SR cover also ions from: Hy-like, He-like, Li-like Na-like, Al-like, Mg-like and Si-like HCIs. Here stands out the Doublet transitions in Na-like ions, produced by the spin-orbit interaction. The Doublet is hard to measure simultaneously for large enough Z, but they are still very interesting because the QED effects also have a strong dependence in Z. “…This measurement tests the predictions of QED for sodium-like ions (D1 and D2 lines at Z=72, 73, 74, and 79.) to more fractional accuracy than even the best results available in hydrogen-like uranium…” In a quote by 2010 JINST 5 C10005 [@10.1088/1748-0221/5/10/C10005]

This research topic had a rapid growth in the 80s, when the EUV to X-ray spectrum of HCIs -from medium and large Z atoms-, was available in smaller scale experimental set ups. The electron beam ion trap (EBIT) had a dominant role, being an ideal plasma device for line identification due to the negligible influence of the Doppler effect. The following comparison is a sample (see table 2 above) of publications in the period 1983 – 2013 on the problem of relativistic corrections and QED on energy levels of HCIs.

sec.title: Transition energies and intensities of transitions on the X-ray spectral range, from highly charged Iron ions (HCI) produced in the laboratory.

p.p: Besides iron (Fe) being the most abundant metal in the Universe, Neon-like Fe XVII is the dominant iron ion over a broad temperature range in coronal equilibrium. Its X-ray emission has been observed in a wide range of astrophysical sources. L-shell emission from Fe XVII, -which falls between 9.8 and 17.5 A- , has been observed in supernova remnants , solar active regions, stellar coronae and X-ray binaries; and it has been extensively studied in order to fully exploit its diagnostic potential. Adapted from [@ 10.1086/305941] Here it is shown relevant laboratory spectrum for Hy-like (Fe XXVI), He-like(Fe XXV), Ne-like (Fe XXVII), Ar-like (Fe IX). Emphasis is made in Dielectronic (DR) transitions (and its ratios) for Hy-like, He-like an Ne-like of Iron (Chandra XRO). DR transitions are a prime candidate to determine electron temperature in hot plasmas. Because of its use in the diagnostics of low- electron density environments, a more recent study case is that of EUV transitions Ar-like Fe IX [@10.3390/ atoms10040115]. Other ions like Fe XVIII – Fe XXV and Fe XII – XIV are also reported. This comparison is a sample (see table 2 above) of publications on the study of the spectrum of Iron (Fe) from HCIs, in the period 1993 – 2022

sec.title: Transition energies and intensities on the UV and visible spectral range, from highly charged ions (HCI) produced in an electron beam ion trap (EBIT).

p.p: This unexpected radiation originates from forbidden transitions of the ground state of HCIs. In 1991 U. Feldman, P. Indelicato, and J. Sugar pointed out that a particular sequence of magnetic dipole (M1) transitions for the Ti-like ions, Xe+32 through U+70, remain relatively constant in the 320–400-nm range[Magnetic dipole line from U lxxi ground-term levels predicted at 3200 ÅJ. Opt. Soc. Am. B 8(1), 3-5 (1991) [@10.1364/JOSAB.8.000003]. This wavelength scaling behavior is very suitable for diagnostics in high energy tokomaks due to its characteristic high ion temperature and low electron density; the later being a favorable condition for the population of the ground state levels. For its very small energy in comparison to the binding energies and its convenient wavelength region, these lines are also suitable for high sensitive tests of atomic structure of HCIs. Discussion partially quoted and adapted from Morgan et a.l 1995 Observation of Visible and UV Magnetic Dipole Transitions in Highly Charged Xenon and Barium, Phys. Rev. Lett. 74, 1716 [@10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.1716]

Besides Ti-like ions other isoelectronicities are referred in this review: Va-like, P-like, Si-like, B-like, and a very extensive compendium of Ar-like to Kr-like by J.R. Crespo Lopez-Urrutia et a. Visible spectrum of highly charged ions: The forbidden optical lines of Kr, Xe, and Ba ions in the Ar I to Kr I isoelectronic sequence Can. J. Phys. [@10.1139/p02-080].

sec.title: Comparison of experimental and calculated values of the energy of x-ray in transitions in heliumlike ions

p.p: This research topic had a rapid growth in the 80s. Most of the measurements in this comparison are from EBIT experiments, however earlier measurements performed in accelerators at various large laboratories are also referred in the comparison. The measurements reported are centered in the well know helium like transitions (E1,w) 1s2p 1P1 →1s2, (M2,x) 1s2p 3P2 →1s2 (E1,y) 1s2p 3P1 →1s2 and (M1,z) 1s2s 3S →1s2 transitions. from He-like ions of : Fe, Ti, V, Cr, Ge, Ar, Kr.

This comparison is a sample (see table 2 above) of publications on the study Comparison of experimental and calculated values of the energy of x-ray in transitions in heliumlike ions, in the period 1982 – 2000.

tr.td: This comparison (4a) responds to a different internal structure, however the glossary shown at the beginning is still valid

The comparison shows a survey of experimental and theoretical values – using 14 contributions- of energies of transitions from two compilation publications Drake et al. [@10.1139/p88-100] and Chantler et al.[@10.1103/PhysRevA.62.042501].

There is a second equivalent version of this comparison(4b) https://orkg.org/comparison/R191978/ can be found in the ORKG. The later is presented in a format where only two contributions are shown; the rest are “hidden but accessible”. The intend of this second version is to display the potions of the ORKG platform.

table-wrap.label: Comparison of experimental and calculated values of the energy of x-ray in transitions in heliumlike ions*

caption.title: Transition energies of highly ionized atoms, is a topic of interest in atomic physics that requires precision measurements from high technology plasma sources and dedicated high resolution x-ray crystal spectrometers. This comparison is a survey experimental and theoretical values of energies of transitions, from ions in the heliumlike sequence. Two compilation publications were used Drake et al. 1988 [ https://doi.org/10.1139/p88-100 ] and Chantler et al. 2000 [ https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.62.042501 ].
